artDirection.style: academic studio-quality cultivation measurement education; cream/neutral background; crisp scientific diagrams; natural plant color where plants are shown; restrained green and gold accents; no yellow cast; no decorative clutter
artDirection.textPolicy: Use short labels, equations, legends and concise callouts. Do not bake paragraph text into the image.
artDirection.accuracyPolicy: Every diagram must distinguish observation from interpretation and method from result. Never imply that extra decimal places equal accuracy or that one sample proves a population claim.
artDirection.accessibilityPolicy: Do not rely on color alone. Every comparison needs text labels, shapes, line styles or position cues, plus descriptive alt text and caption.
artDirection.copyrightPolicy: Create original educational artwork. Source material constrains concepts and terminology; do not reproduce published figures.
artDirection.reviewPolicy: Artwork remains brief-approved-artwork-needed until scientific QA, visual QA, label/spelling QA, accessibility QA and page-placement QA all pass.

briefs.primaryMessage: Accuracy, precision, resolution and uncertainty are different properties. A display can be highly repeatable or show many decimal places while still being biased or uncertain.
layout: Top title band: ACCURACY, PRECISION, RESOLUTION & UNCERTAINTY
Four target-style panels: accurate + precise; accurate + imprecise; precise + biased; imprecise + biased
Instrument display inset contrasting fine display resolution with a wider stated accuracy specification
Uncertainty bar example around a measured value
Bottom decision strip: Measure → Compare to reference → Report supported digits → Preserve uncertainty
requiredCallouts: Repeatable does not automatically mean correct
More decimal places do not prove accuracy
Report uncertainty appropriate to the method
forbiddenClaims: Do not present precision and accuracy as synonyms
Do not imply instrument resolution equals measurement accuracy
Do not imply uncertainty can be removed entirely by repeated measurements
briefs.altText: Educational target-style comparison of accuracy and precision, plus an instrument display example showing that resolution and decimal places do not equal accuracy, with a simple uncertainty interval.
briefs.caption: Measurement quality depends on accuracy, precision, bias, resolution and uncertainty. Extra digits are not evidence that the underlying measurement is more correct.

scientific: All four accuracy/precision combinations are correct
Bias is explicitly distinguished from random spread
Resolution is not labeled as accuracy
visual: Targets remain readable at mobile size
No interpretation depends on color alone
Neutral background and no yellow cast

briefs.primaryMessage: Calibration and reference checks connect sensor output to known standards and reveal drift before crop decisions are based on bad data.
layout: Top title band: CALIBRATION, DRIFT & REFERENCE CHECKS
Left workflow: inspect/clean → known standard → pre-check reading → adjustment if method allows → post-check → log
Center time-series showing gradual sensor drift away from a maintained reference
Right paired-sensor cross-check showing persistent offset versus random noise
Bottom calibration record strip with date, standard, temperature, pre/post deviation, operator and maintenance
requiredCallouts: Calibration is part of the measurement method
A stable wrong reading is still wrong
Investigate persistent offsets before changing crop settings
forbiddenClaims: Do not imply every sensor can or should be manually adjusted
Do not prescribe one universal calibration interval
Do not show a reference sensor as infallible
briefs.altText: Measurement workflow showing inspection, known-standard calibration, post-check verification, long-term sensor drift compared with a maintained reference, and the fields needed in a calibration log.
briefs.caption: Reference checks and calibration help separate real environmental change from sensor drift, contamination, aging or persistent instrument offset.

scientific: Reference comparison is shown as quality control rather than proof of truth
visual: Drift and offset are distinguishable without color

briefs.queueTitle: Sensor Placement, Canopy Grid & Representative Sampling
briefs.primaryMessage: Sensor location is part of the measurement definition. Repeatable spatial grids reveal canopy gradients that one convenient sensor or room average can hide.
layout: Top-down grow-room/canopy plan with coordinate grid and labeled sample points
Side elevation showing canopy height, above-canopy, within-canopy and biased wall/fixture/HVAC positions
Raw-value grid example retained beside a derived heat-map style summary
Small sampling panel contrasting fixed sentinel points with randomized plant/leaf sampling
Bottom metadata strip: coordinate, height, stage, timestamp, nearby source/obstruction
requiredCallouts: A room average can hide hotspots and dead zones
Reuse the same grid after system changes
Keep raw grid values, not only a heat map
forbiddenClaims: Do not present one sensor location as universally correct for every variable
Do not imply a heat map is raw data
Do not use unlabeled decorative sensor icons
briefs.altText: Top-down and side-view cultivation measurement diagram showing a repeatable canopy sensor grid, representative and biased locations, raw spatial values, sentinel points and randomized sampling positions.
briefs.caption: Sensor placement and sampling geometry determine what is measured. A documented spatial grid exposes gradients and makes before-after comparisons repeatable.

scientific: Position and height are treated as method metadata
Raw values are retained separately from visual interpolation
Sentinel and random sampling are distinguished
visual: Top-down and side-view geometry are easy to separate
All coordinates and height cues are readable

briefs.queueTitle: Baseline, Control, Treatment, Randomization & Position Effects
briefs.primaryMessage: A useful cultivation trial defines a pre-change baseline, a comparison group, treatment assignment and position strategy before the outcome is interpreted.
layout: Top timeline: baseline period → assignment → intervention → observation window → recheck/decision
Bench map contrasting confounded left-versus-right treatment placement with randomized or blocked placement
Control and treatment plants shown under the same measurement schedule
Confounder callout showing simultaneous light, irrigation and nutrient changes destroying attribution
Bottom rule strip: one major learning variable when practical; document emergency stacked changes as attribution-limited
requiredCallouts: Before-after alone is weaker than a contemporaneous control
forbiddenClaims: Do not imply every production decision requires a formal randomized trial
Do not imply randomization eliminates every source of bias
Do not present correlation as a treatment effect
briefs.altText: Cultivation experiment diagram showing a baseline-to-treatment timeline, control and treatment groups, confounded bench placement versus randomized or blocked placement, and how multiple simultaneous changes limit causal interpretation.
briefs.caption: Baselines, controls and treatment assignment make cultivation comparisons more interpretable. Position effects and stacked changes can otherwise masquerade as treatment responses.

scientific: Baseline and contemporaneous control are distinguished
Randomization and blocking are presented accurately
Confounding from stacked changes is explicit
visual: Timeline and bench layout can be understood independently
Control/treatment distinction does not rely on color only

briefs.primaryMessage: Diagnostic images become comparable evidence only when identity, tissue location, scale, lighting, capture conditions and scoring rules are standardized.
layout: Top title band: STANDARDIZED IMAGING & SCORING
Three-shot capture set: whole plant overview, affected-organ context, close detail with physical scale
Good-versus-poor lighting comparison showing neutral white balance versus colored/blurple or filtered image
Metadata card: plant ID, cultivar, date/time, node/tissue, camera/magnification, lighting, original filename
Anchored 1–5 ordinal scoring strip with written definitions for each level
Bottom reminder: observation field separate from diagnosis/hypothesis field
requiredCallouts: Color shifts can create or hide symptoms
A score is reproducible only when its anchors are defined
forbiddenClaims: Do not imply a photograph alone proves a diagnosis
Do not show a 1–5 scale without written anchors
briefs.altText: Standardized cultivation imaging protocol showing whole-plant, tissue-context and close-up photographs with scale, neutral lighting, metadata fields, unedited-original retention and an anchored ordinal scoring rubric.
briefs.caption: Consistent capture conditions, identity, scale and scoring anchors make images useful for comparison. Observation should be recorded separately from diagnosis or interpretation.

scientific: Observation and interpretation are visibly separated
White balance is framed as a comparability issue
Ordinal anchors are defined rather than just numbered
visual: Good/poor image example does not depend on hue alone
placement: Diagnostic Index and GrowLens cross-reference after approval

briefs.primaryMessage: Repeated measurements, independent biological replicates, uncertainty and causal reasoning determine how strongly cultivation evidence can support a conclusion.
layout: Top-left comparison: five leaves on one plant = technical/subsample evidence versus five independent plants = biological replication
Top-right distribution plot showing individual values, mean/median and spread rather than a single bar
Center correlation panel showing two variables moving together with three explanations: A causes B, B causes A, third factor influences both
Bottom evidence chain: raw observation → method/metadata → comparison → interpretation + uncertainty → bounded action → recheck
Confidence marker showing low/medium/high confidence tied to evidence quality, not visual certainty
requiredCallouts: Multiple leaves on one plant are not multiple independent plants
Correlation alone does not establish cause
Uncertainty should change confidence and the next test
forbiddenClaims: Do not imply more observations automatically fix biased sampling
Do not imply statistical significance equals practical importance
Do not imply correlation proves causation
briefs.altText: Statistical-thinking diagram comparing biological and technical replication, showing individual-data spread, alternative explanations for correlation, and an evidence chain from raw observation through uncertainty-aware action and recheck.
briefs.caption: Replication, sample structure, spread and uncertainty determine how strongly evidence supports a conclusion. Correlation alone cannot identify cause.

scientific: Experimental units and subsamples are distinguished correctly
Individual values and spread are retained
visual: Evidence chain has a clear direction
Confidence is not encoded by color alone
